Subject: Log export: retention windows and signed URL process

Hi Karthik,

Quick context: our auditors asked for a detailed explanation of how Redwood handles audit/access log exports for tenants. They want to know:
- What retention windows you support for audit and access logs (minimum/maximum and configurable options)
- Export mechanisms (can you push to our S3, or provide presigned URLs / SCP / SFTP?)
- Export formats and manifest contents (do you include checksums, tenant IDs, time slices?)
- How deletion is handled after retention expires, and whether you can provide an attestation/certification for deletion

Also, can you provide a sample manifest (CSV or JSON) so we can show the auditors what the export looks like? Ideally we’d get something by EOD Monday (May 16).

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers up front, details below and I'll loop in Neha for the technical specifics and the export manifest sample.

High level:
- Retention: configurable per-tenant; standard options are 90, 180, 365, and 730 days; we also support custom retention up to 7 years for enterprise contracts and legal-hold exceptions.
- Exports: we support both push-to-customer (we can write directly to your S3 via a customer-provided IAM role) and pull-style exports (pre-signed S3 URLs). We also support SFTP in limited regions.
- Formats: exports are available as compressed JSONL or Parquet; each export bundle includes a manifest with record counts, CRC32 checksums, tenant_id mapping, time-range, and schema version.
- Deletion attestations: when retention expires (and no legal hold), we can produce a deletion certificate indicating which files were removed and a hash manifest of what was deleted.

Attachment: audit_export_playbook_v1.pdf — high-level runbook. Neha will add the manifest and a short example.

Propose a 30-minute call tomorrow (May 15) to walk the auditors through the sample if that helps.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stokes <alex.stokes@finhealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-14T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Log export: retention windows and signed URL process

Hi Alex / Karthik — Neha here (Security Ops). Adding the technical detail Alex requested and a small sample manifest attached. See inline for specifics.

Export formats and manifest contents:
- Bundles: We produce time-sliced bundles (default slice = 6 hours; can be configured 1h/6h/24h). Bundles are delivered as .jsonl.gz or .parquet.snappy.
- Manifest file (CSV or JSON): includes columns/keys: tenant_id, bundle_start_ts, bundle_end_ts, record_count, uncompressed_size_bytes, crc32_checksum, md5_bundle, schema_version, export_job_id.
- Tenant mapping: each log entry has a tenant_id field; manifest also contains an anonymized tenant alias column if customers need obfuscation.

Delivery options and security:
- Push-to-S3: preferred — customer provides an S3 bucket and a cross-account IAM role with PutObject and PutObjectAcl permissions. We stream directly into your bucket and emit a final manifest.
- Pre-signed URLs: we can generate time-limited (configurable TTL) presigned PUT URLs if you prefer us to upload to an intermediate store and you pull.
- Encryption: all data at rest is encrypted by customer KMS (you can provide a key) or our managed KMS; transport uses HTTPS/TLS 1.2+.
- Access controls: exports are written with server-side encryption and ACLs set to private; we rotate the temporary credentials used for uploads per job.

Deletion and attestation process:
1) Deletion trigger: when a bundle reaches end-of-retention and no legal hold, bundle is marked for deletion.
2) Deletion workflow: files are removed from primary storage and tombstoned in metadata with a deletion record. For cloud object storage we perform a coordinated delete + manifest update.
3) Attestation: within 5 business days we can produce an attestation report that lists file names, checksums, deletion timestamps, and a signed hash chain (PKI-signed). For enterprise contracts we can shorten SLA to 2 business days.
4) Legal holds: we support hold flags per-tenant that pause deletions and preserve bundles until hold is released.

Notes and exclusions:
- KV cache snapshots and ephemeral inference caches are NOT part of audit/access log exports by default; if you need them we can scope a separate snapshot export (requires additional entitlements).
- Personally identifiable fields in logs: we follow the data minimization agreed in the DPA. If you need field-level redaction in export manifests, we can enable that during job configuration.

Example presigned PUT (partial):
curl -X PUT "https://s3.amazonaws.com/your-bucket/bundles/tenant123/20280514-00-06.jsonl.gz?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&..." -H "x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms" --upload-file bundle.jsonl.gz

Attachment: sample_manifest_20280514.csv (attached) — small sample with three bundles.

Happy to run through a live sample export to your bucket. If you can share an S3 role ARN or a test bucket we can schedule the export.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security Operations, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

2) Can Redwood run the export job directly into our S3 (preferred) or do we need to run a pull? If you can run it, confirm the SLA for the deletion attestation (we'd prefer 2 business days if possible).

Alex — quick confirmation and next steps:

1) Tenant mapping: yes — the manifest includes tenant_id and an account_id column compatible with common SIEM ingestion. We'll provide field names and a short mapping doc.

2) Export execution: we can run the export directly into your S3 bucket using a cross-account IAM role. If you share a test bucket ARN plus an IAM role we can use, we'll kick off a one-off export. We can also provide presigned PUTs if you prefer to pull.

3) Deletion attestation SLA: standard is 5 business days; for enterprise customers we can commit to 2 business days in contract and will commit to providing a one-off historical attestation for the prior 12 months within 10 business days (reasonable effort; may require a scoped discovery to locate archived bundles).

Attachments provided: sample_manifest_20280514.csv (example manifest), audit_export_playbook_v1.pdf (runbook).

- Please share a test S3 bucket ARN and a cross-account role (or let us know if you prefer presigned URLs).
- If the auditor wants, we can set a 30-minute session next week to walk through the manifest fields with your SIEM team.
- Karthik will follow up with a short mapping doc and the HubSpot link to the deal.
